Definition: from G1537 and G1651; to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish:--convince.
BiblicalUsage: Exelencho means to convict fully, and it stands in John 8:9, where those who heard Jesus are convicted by their own conscience and slip away one by one. The verse stands in the passage about the woman taken in adultery, which the SBL text does not carry, so it is a Textus Receptus reading.
TheologicalSignificance: I take exelencho as it stands: to convict fully.
